      <title>ANC faces anger over poor services as South Africans vote in local elections</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/04/anc-south-africa-local-elections-water-outages-power-cuts</link>
      <description><p>Party expected to get less than a third of the vote amid frustration over water outages and power cuts</p><p>The African National Congress is on course for a bruising result in South Africa’s local elections on Wednesday as voters go to the polls amid deep discontent over water outages, power cuts and crumbling infrastructure.</p><p>The former liberation movement, which Nelson Mandela led to power in 1994 at the end of apartheid as South Africa’s first black president, is still likely to be the largest party. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Wed, 04 Nov 2026 11:53:11 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category></category><title>What consequences for Israel as Democrats win the US midterm elections?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261104-what-consequences-for-israel-as-democrats-win-the-us-midterm-elections</link><description>
Democrats seized control of the US Congress on Tuesday, capturing the Senate and House of Representatives in a stunning upset. What are the potential consequences for Israel and Benjamin Netanyahu, as Trump announced on Tuesday that the US will halt $3.8 billion in aid to the country? FRANCE 24's correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky has more.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6b47fad2-d840-11f1-946b-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-fb7d0638.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6b47fad2-d840-11f1-946b-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-fb7d0638.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c120a2f2-d83f-11f1-9e94-61d3912dca56</guid><pubDate>Wed, 04 Nov 2026 11:32:43 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>US midterms: Trump reacts to the Democrats’ sweeping victory</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261104-us-midterms-trump-reacts-to-the-democrats-sweeping-victory</link><description>
US President Donald Trump had rare praise for rival Democrats Tuesday after their stunning US midterm elections victory and admitted the Iran war may have played a part in the defeat of his Republican Party. But the 80-year-old refused to take any personal responsibility for the result.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6fd0ce66-d841-11f1-9a33-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/mini1-3.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6fd0ce66-d841-11f1-9a33-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/mini1-3.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a067e226-d841-11f1-9cb6-2fded3235c75</guid><pubDate>Wed, 04 Nov 2026 11:24:24 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Ethiopia expands hydropower ambitions</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261104-ethiopia-expands-hydropower-ambitions</link><description>
Ethiopia is looking to position itself as an African leader in clean energy, as it prepares to host next year’s COP32 climate summit. Alongside the GERD, the country is building another massive hydropower project on the Omo River in the southwest, as it expands electricity production and exports power to neighbouring countries. This report from our correspondent Tom Canetti.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e47e37a4-d840-11f1-8a58-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261029-155341-155532-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e47e37a4-d840-11f1-8a58-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261029-155341-155532-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e8f6290e-d840-11f1-b059-75caf87c0edc</guid><pubDate>Wed, 04 Nov 2026 11:19:36 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>From Kansas to Texas, Democrats win big in Republican heartlands</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261104-from-kansas-to-texas-democrats-win-big-in-republican-heartlands</link><description>
The Democrats are set to take control of both the House and the Senate following victories in states like South Carolina, Kansas, and Texas, whose switching blue constitutes an historic upset. President Donald Trump has said he will accept the results and blames the candidates themselves for the losses.

]]> <![CDATA[ The Taurid meteor shower peaks tonight — and fireballs could steal the show ]]> Heads up stargazers! The Taurid meteor shower is upon us, bringing multiple peaks of activity that could see spectacular shooting stars and fireballs brighten November's sky. Here's where and when to look.

What is the Taurid meteor shower(s)?

Every autumn, Earth plows through streams of debris left behind by Comet Encke, a 3-mile-wide (4.8-kilometer) ice body that orbits the sun once every 3.3 years.

These debris streams produce two branches of the Taurid meteor shower: The Southern Taurids, active from Sept. 20 to Nov. 20 and the Northern Taurids, active from Oct. 20 to Dec. 10.

As Earth plows through the debris streams, tiny particles slam into our atmosphere at 65,000 miles per hour (104,607 kilometers per hour), producing dazzling streaks of light across the night sky.

Both branches of the Taurid meteor shower appear to travel away from a point of origin — or radiant — located in the constellation Taurus, which rises in the southeastern sky during November evenings.

The Taurids are known for spawning brilliant fireball meteors, which can flare brighter than Venus as pebble-sized pieces of debris enter and burn up in the atmosphere.

When to look for Taurid shooting stars

The Southern Taurid shower features two distinct yearly peaks, the first of which occurred on Oct. 14. The second takes place overnight on Nov. 4-5 and is associated with an increase in fireball activity, when up to five meteors per hour could be seen blazing across the sky.

The Northern Taurid stream, meanwhile, is expected to peak overnight on Nov. 11-12 with the same predicted hourly rate of up to five meteors per hour streaking across the dark, near moonless sky.

How to spot Taurid meteors

Head out to a dark sky location around midnight on the night of the peaks, when the shower's radiant in the constellation Taurus is positioned high in the southeastern sky, maximizing the number of meteors that can be seen.

Remember not to stare directly at the radiant. Meteors seen close to the constellation Taurus strike our planet almost head-on, and so will have the shortest trails. Instead, pick out a patch of sky a little distance away, where the shooting stars will be at their most eye-catching as they skim through Earth's atmosphere.

Never use a telescope or binoculars to hunt for meteors, you want to take in as much of the sky as possible, not limit your field of view! And be sure to wrap up warm and allow 20-30 minutes for your eyes to adapt to the dark — a vital and often overlooked step for anyone hoping to catch even the faintest of meteors.

]]> <![CDATA[ NASA asks industry for ideas about saving Hubble Space Telescope ]]> NASA is reviving discussions to rescue the Hubble Space Telescope, which is operating well but is on track to reenter Earth's atmosphere about six years from now.

The agency issued a request for information (RFI) on Oct. 29 for "in-space servicing" capabilities, which could include boosting Hubble's orbit (which is naturally degrading due to atmospheric drag), or even a mission to "enhance its capabilities" in some way.

Hubble, which launched in April 1990 in partnership with the European Space Agency, was serviced five times by astronauts on space shuttle missions, the most recent being in 2009. The observatory's groundbreaking achievements include helping to show that the expansion of the universe is accelerating — a discovery that won the Nobel Prize — as well as a swath of finds about planets, galaxies, stars and other parts of the universe.

Hubble also regularly teams up with other telescopes for science work, and its observations have led to the publication of at least 23,000 scientific papers, NASA figures suggest. And, despite its age, Hubble remains in high demand. "Astronomers request about seven times as much observing time as is available each year," the agency stated in September.

Hubble is also widely appreciated by the public. People have long enjoyed and celebrated its iconic images, such as the Eagle Nebula's "Pillars of Creation," a gorgeous shot that has been revisited several times over the decades. As such, this is not the first time in recent years that discussions have opened about keeping the famed observatory running for a while longer.

In 2022, for example, billionaire tech entrepreneur Jared Isaacman proposed using SpaceX hardware to mount a Hubble-servicing mission. (Isaacman also purchased and commanded two crewed SpaceX missions to Earth orbit, which flew in September 2021 and September 2024.) NASA declined, however, citing possible risks to the healthy observatory.

]]> <![CDATA[ Ancient star collisions could explain mysterious Little Red Dots and 'impossible' black holes ]]> New research suggests that collisions between stars in the early universe were common, which could help explain the rapid growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST).

The team behind this research performed simulations of the early universe and found stellar systems were densely packed, leading to stars frequently slamming into each other. While rapid collisions would have destroyed the stars involved, slower collisions would have led to repeated mergers, creating single over-massive stars, which could collapse and form larger-than-usual black holes at the end of their lives. These could be the seeds of the first supermassive black holes.

Dense stellar environments do still exist in the modern universe at the hearts of galaxies; however, these aren't conducive to the types of collisions that would birth ultra-massive stars. That is because there are already supermassive black holes at the hearts of modern galaxies, and their immense gravitational influence speeds up orbiting stars, meaning collisions that do occur are high-speed and destructive, thus failing to birth overmassive stars.

"Perhaps the strangest outcome of our simulations is that stars can merge repeatedly within the cluster until they form one gigantic star with a mass equal to that of an entire cluster," team member Claire Williams, of the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), said in a statement. "When a star this huge reaches the end of its life, models suggest that it may have no option but to collapse into itself and form a massive black hole."

My, haven't you grown? How did supermassive black holes get so big so fast?

The existence of supermassive black holes before the universe was even 1 billion years old is something that has puzzled astronomers since the JWST started spotting them in 2022.

This is because black holes should need at least 1 billion years to complete the feeding and merger processes that result in a "supermassive" status of possessing millions or billions of times the mass of the sun.

One suggestion put forward by scientists to explain this is that supermassive black holes don't start out from scratch. Instead, they form from black hole seeds called intermediate-mass black holes.

Normally, when a massive star collapses, it births a stellar-mass black hole possessing a mass between 10 and 100 times the mass of the sun. This is considerably smaller than supermassive black holes that dominate the hearts of all modern galaxies with masses millions to billions of times the mass of our star.

Intermediate-mass black holes are thought to sit between these two families of cosmic titans with masses between 100 and 100,000 times that of the sun. The problem is, no single star should have enough mass to collapse and create an intermediate-mass black hole. But that is valid only for the conditions we see in the "modern" 13.8-billion-year-old universe in our immediate cosmic vicinity. Conditions were very different further out into the universe and further back in time.

Indeed, such seeds emerged from these new simulations in environments of dense star clustering, which could solve this mystery by allowing those growth processes to get a head start.

"Dense star clusters provide a natural birthplace for massive black-hole seeds in our model," Williams said. "The same environment that forms the black hole can also provide stars and gas that influence its subsequent growth."

However, this could be a two-for-one deal. The JWST has also been routinely discovering astronomical bodies called Little Red Dots in the early universe. Little Red Dots are curious because they seem to have completely disappeared by the time the cosmos reached 2 billion years old.

Little Red Dots the cosmic elephant in the room

Little Red Dots are extremely compact objects in the early universe that get their moniker from the fact that they look like red dots.

"Little Red Dots are a hot topic in astronomy. You can compare studies of people trying to understand Little Red Dots to the tale of blind people who are trying to describe an elephant by touching it, and each person describes it differently based on what part they’re touching," team member and UCLA researcher Smadar Naoz said. "Our research connects several of those perspectives together and may help us see more of the elephant."

There have been many suggestions about the true nature of these objects, but one theory suggests that they possess a rapidly growing black hole at their hearts.

The team's simulations suggest that Little Red Dots may be dense star clusters that are constantly being rocked by repeated stellar collisions. This results in a very large star, which eventually collapses to become an intermediate-mass black hole.

But if that is the case, why were there no Little Red Dots around to celebrate the 2 billionth birthday of the universe?

Less than 1 billion years after the Big Bang, the universe was devoid of well-ordered spiral galaxies, but was instead filled with dense and chaotic clusters of star birth. As these regions were rocked with frequent star collisions, the conditions were right for ultra-massive stars to form and collapse into intermediate-mass black holes.

However, as the universe cooled and expanded, these sites became the building blocks of far less chaotic galaxies. Thus, if Little Red Dots are chaotic star clusters needed to form intermediate-mass black holes, progress toward an equilibrium state could explain why they suddenly disappeared from the universe. The cosmos just wasn't extreme enough to maintain Little Red Dots anymore.

The team's research was published on Monday (Oct. 26) in the Astrophysical Journal.

]]> <![CDATA[ Voting in space: NASA astronauts cast ballots from International Space Station ]]> The three Americans currently living off Earth just made sure their electoral voices were heard.

Anil Menon told us today (Nov. 3) that he and fellow NASA astronauts Luke Delaney and Jessica Watkins voted in the U.S. midterm elections from the International Space Station (ISS).

"Yes, you can even vote from space! All three U.S. crew members had the privilege of voting from space station. We filled out an electronic ballot and sent it securely to the election officials," Menon wrote in an X post this morning.

That post included a 29-second video, in which Menon — wearing, like many of us today, an "I voted" sticker — shows us his "voting booth."

It's actually his room on the ISS, Menon explained. "Inside of it is my computer, where I was able to fill out an electronic form and send it to Harris County so I could vote today," he said.

Most NASA astronauts register to vote in Texas' Harris County; it's home to Johnson Space Center in Houston, the agency's human spaceflight hub.

Americans have been able to vote from space since 1997, when Texas passed a law allowing this to happen. The first person to take advantage of the legislation was NASA astronaut David Wolf, who cast his ballot from Russia's Mir space station that same year. (The ISS didn't welcome its first crew until November 2000.)

"Just like any other American away from home, astronauts may fill out a Federal Post Card Application to request an absentee ballot," NASA officials wrote in an astronaut-voting explainer.

The process is somewhat involved, however.

"After an astronaut fills out an electronic ballot aboard the orbiting laboratory, the document flows through NASA's Tracking and Data Relay Satellite System to a ground antenna at the agency's White Sands Test Facility in Las Cruces, New Mexico," they added. "From New Mexico, NASA transfers the ballot to the Mission Control Center at NASA Johnson and then on to the county clerk responsible for casting the ballot. To preserve the vote's integrity, the ballot is encrypted and accessible only by the astronaut and the clerk."

Delaney and Watkins launched to the ISS on Oct. 1 on SpaceX's Crew-13 mission. Menon has been there since mid-July, arriving aboard a Russian Soyuz spacecraft.

The trio currently share the orbiting lab with four other people — Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk and cosmonauts Anna Kikina, Pyotr Dubrov and Sergey Teteryatnikov. Kutryk and Teteryatnikov are members of Crew-13, whereas Dubrov and Kikina shared the Soyuz with Menon.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'OGame' developers explain how the browser-based sci-fi game has lasted 24 years ahead of the huge Orion update ]]> If you were on the Internet in the early 2000s looking for free browser games to play, OGame was a blooming sci-fi strategy sensation that couldn't be ignored. With online servers providing the structure for a living and evolving universe where players fought, traded, and created empires from scratch, its limited visual presentation was no issue.

Times have changed, but GameForge hasn't gone anywhere. OGame has been ported to mobile devices, and content updates have kept it alive and fresh for much longer than a plethora of installable MMO games.

With the Orion update, which will hit the newly launched universes (servers) on November 6, OGame is introducing conflicts against non-player-character (NPC) enemies, wave-based battles, co-op missions, and completely new systems that can also be disrupted by other players.

The game's endurance and such a major reinvention are stunning achievements, so we asked GameForge's Martin Liedtke (Director, Products of Browser Games) and Enrico Mareth (Senior Project Manager for OGame PC and Mobile) about the many challenges of working on OGame alongside the community for so long, what Orion is bringing to the table, and what's next for this worldwide phenomenon.

Some quotes have been editorialized and lightly trimmed for better flow.

"OGame has an enduring core: You build an interstellar empire, and your decisions matter... Keeping it fresh means adding meaningful choices to that foundation," said Liedtke. "Orion adds missions against automated opponents (PvE) alongside missions open to other players (PvP)... It supports different appetites for risk."

The GameForge veteran noted, however, that it's the community that "supplies another kind of freshness" after the studio releases the new content. "We develop the systems; players create much of the history."

Part of this approach is keeping tabs on how very different kinds of players approach what's available. "Some commanders concentrate on their economy; others enjoy expeditions or carefully coordinated fleet operations... Orion follows that approach; more experienced players can dig into fleet composition, progression, and cooperation. The aim is to offer worthwhile choices."

Liedtke also noted that "OGame's PvP has become a sophisticated contest of information and coordination" over time. Some players like to scout targets and organize combined attacks when enemy fleets are vulnerable. Those battles resolve automatically, but it's the planning that "can be remarkably intricate," especially after so many years of updates.

The PvE in Orion doesn't sacrifice any of those intricacies or density. In fact, it's adding a "more structured layer" that gives players clear objectives. In most cases, they'll have to cooperate to obtain better rewards. "There is a strong case for introducing that kind of cooperative PvE earlier. It gives players another reason to build and use fleets together."

Over two decades later, how people choose to engage with OGame has changed, pushing GameForge to consider supporting new platforms. Today, mobile devices have become essential to free-to-play games' success over time.

Mareth told us their importance "has made touch controls, navigation, and clarity on smaller screens central development considerations," even if thousands of players still remain attached to PC as their main platform. "We're currently working on a design overhaul of the app, combining what we've learned with players' feedback."

Liedtke also said there is more overlap between PC and mobile players than you might imagine.

"The same player might check their empire on a phone and spend a longer session planning in the browser." Liedtke also noted that "Different playstyles also have different needs," adding that activities like mining and trading fit "comfortably" into short mobile sessions, but complex fleet operations benefit from sitting in front of one's PC.

While it's a game of interstellar conflict and sci-fi spaceships, OGame does take a lot of inspiration from real-life science, even if it stretches that science well past its limits. "When ships are destroyed in battle, the debris field can form a moon around a player's planet," explains Liedtke. "The chance (of that happening) is linked to the real lunar cycle: it is higher around a full moon than a new moon."

He noted it's a "playful connection" to astronomy, "rather than a simulation of how real moons form," but the developers thought it was cool to influence the game via things that happen in our own sky.

This possible in-game "event" also led to one of the best examples of player ingenuity in OGame: Moonshots. Liedtke explained that "players organize deliberate battles and exchange sacrificial fleets to help one another obtain those valuable moons. They have turned destruction into a cooperative project. For a designer, the lesson is to examine what players can achieve together, as well as what an individual action rewards."

As the team figured out how to develop "the more imaginative side of science fiction" in OGame's universe, they also decided to explicitly use deuterium for fusion research and as fuel. Star Trek fans will recognize this as the starship fuel of that universe, but it is a real substance: one of two stable isotopes of hydrogen. "Those scientific references give the universe familiar foundations," remarks Liedtke.

In OGame's shared galaxy, Orion is introducing "anomalies" as a central new feature, which Liedtke described as "mission sites you uncover with a new scanner" before it's required to send in ships. "Combat missions ask you to hold position against waves of automated fleets; peaceful missions put your cargo ships to work collecting rewards." The twist is these missions are open to co-op... but also to rival commanders that can attack the objectives marked as PvP. While you can theoretically ignore them, better rewards await for daring commanders.

With PvE bringing all sorts of new design opportunities to the table, Liedtke pointed out the Orion update "gives us a foundation to learn which kinds of missions players find rewarding" as GameForge looks to the strategy MMO's future. "Personally, I would like to explore encounters that make commanders reconsider what to send and how to work together. Discovery becomes more interesting when it changes your plan."

Sounds exciting, though Liedtke quickly added that this isn't an official announcement of future features.

OGame's 25th anniversary is in 2027, and while the team is tight-lipped on what the team has planned, Liedtke noted that "Reaching a quarter of a century in 2027 will be an extraordinary moment for OGame. We owe that longevity to the team's continued work and, above all, to the players who keep building empires, forming alliances, and giving this universe its stories."

OGame is available on PC (via browser and GameForge's own platform) and on mobile devices via the App Store and Google Play. The Orion update arrives on November 6, 2026.

]]> <![CDATA[ Hubble Telescope sees cosmic 'cat's tail' that could wrap around Earth and the sun 500 times ]]> Using the Hubble Space Telescope, astronomers have investigated a cosmic cat's tail, finding it likely formed after two Pluto-sized bodies smashed together.

The feature, nicknamed the Cat's Tail, extends out from the debris disk known as Beta Pictoris which is located in a planetary system located 63 light-years away. This tail would put that of the average tabby to shame: It's so long that it could curl around the sun-Earth system about 500 times. That's about as long as 200 trillion house cats.

The major difference between our solar system and the planetary system that hosts the Cat's Tail is the latter's relative youth. While our solar system is around 4.6 billion years old, Beta Pictoris is a cosmic kitten no more than a few million years old. That means it is still host to collisions between planetary bodies similar to the ones that rocked the solar system during its infancy.

The team behind this research gained new insights into the Cat's Tail using 14 years of observations. This allowed them to solve the long-standing mystery of the violent conditions under which it formed.

"The Cat's Tail is thought to be the aftermath of a collision between large bodies — think something like Pluto," team leader Arin Avsar of the University of Arizona said in a statement. "Oddly, this feature had previously only been seen with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), which detects infrared light, but remained invisible at shorter wavelengths, which has puzzled the community for a while."

Cosmic cat tail is also pleasingly fluffy

Comparing Beta Pictoris and our solar system, one thing rapidly becomes apparent: our cosmic neighborhood is relatively well-ordered. The planets orbit the sun with most space rocks neatly delegated into bands: the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter, and the Kuiper belt out beyond the orbit of Neptune.

However, this is a stark contrast to the solar system's violent and chaotic youth. Back then, the solar system was host to an infant star surrounded by a swirling disk of gas and dust in which collisions between bodies called planetesimals — the building blocks of planets — were commonplace.

Astronomers can't look back to the solar system's infancy, so to learn more about how our cosmic backyard took shape, they study nearby young planetary systems. Systems like Beta Pictoris. That doesn't mean it has been quick to divulge its secrets, though.

"We think the Cat's Tail has eluded our observations in visible light until now because of what it's made of," Avsar explained. "It consists almost entirely of what we call organic refractory material, which is heavily carbon-based. These long chains of carbon atoms absorb visible light, so they're quite black."

This new study revealed that the feline feature is cat-like in more ways than just its shape. It's also pleasingly fluffy, Hubble observations suggest. That's because the grains that compose it are extremely porous.

"How you can get dust grains that small that are as porous as we see here no one really understands, and that's part of why we study this feature," Avsar said.

"It's possible that the velocities involved in the collisions were so high that the carbon grains vaporized, turned into gas, and then recondensed as they cooled, and that's how they became so porous," team member Kevin Wagner of the U of A said.

The scientists also discovered a hitherto undiscovered feature in the Cat's Tail — a warp that seems to be the result of an interaction between the trail of material and one of the planets in the system, Beta Pictoris b, a gas giant planet 10 times more massive than Jupiter.

"This gives us another line of evidence into how giant planets influence comets through their immense gravitational force," Avsar said. "It's a testament to how much these massive planets really influence their surrounding dust and icy bodies out to hundreds of astronomical units [one astronomical unit being the distance between Earth and the sun]."

The team's research was published last month in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

]]> <![CDATA[ The 2027 'eclipse of the century' will plunge real Star Wars filming locations into darkness ]]> On Aug. 2, 2027, the moon's shadow will sweep across some of the most iconic filming locations from Star Wars, plunging them into darkness during what's being called the "eclipse of the century".

The path of the 2027 total solar eclipse will cross southern Tunisia, where several locations were used to bring the fictional desert planet Tatooine to life. From the dunes of Mos Espa to the rocky Jundland Wastes, Star Wars fans will have the rare opportunity to experience totality at the very places where their favorite scenes were filmed

But not every famous filming location will experience totality, so choosing where to watch will be crucial. Here are four locations that fall directly in the moon's shadow. All times, totality durations and historical cloud cover data come from Time and Date.

1. Eriguet dunes (Mos Espa)

Location: south of Chott el-Gharsa, Tozeur Governorate, southwest Tunisia

Start of totality and duration: 10:06 a.m. CET; 2 minutes, 9 seconds

Chance of clouds: 2%

With a massive budget and three prequels to make, Lucasfilm built a new film set that would double as the Mos Espa spaceport on Tatooine for The Phantom Menace and Attack of the Clones. This is where Qui-Gon Jinn, Obi-Wan Kenobi, Jar Jar Binks and Padme get stranded, where they meet Anakin Skywalker and where the podrace takes place. Now abandoned, it's in the middle of nowhere, between two huge salt lakes and subject to the intense heat and moving Eriguet dunes — but it is firmly within the path of totality. Nearby are two other shooting locations — the Ong Jemel outcrop, where Darth Maul arrives on the scene, and Yardang, where Qui-Gon and Darth Maul battle — the first-ever lightsaber duel filmed on location.

2. Maguer Gorge (Jundland Wastes)

Location: Jebel Sidi Bouhlel canyon, Dghoumès National Park, Tozeur, southwest Tunisia

Start of totality and duration: 10:06 a.m. CET; 3 minutes, 37 seconds

Chance of clouds: 1%

Often called "Star Wars Canyon" by fans and crew, Maguer Gorge in Jebel Sidi Bouhlel doubled as the Jundland Wastes of Tatooine in Star Wars: Episode IV — A New Hope. It's where Luke Skywalker is attacked by Tusken Raiders, where Obi-Wan Kenobi first appears and where Luke and Obi-Wan discover the slaughtered Jawas. The canyon also provided the distant view of Mos Eisley — the famous "wretched hive of scum and villainy." On Aug. 2, 2027, you'll likely be pointing your macrobinoculars at the eclipsed sun rather than Tusken Raiders.

Steven Spielberg later filmed here for Raiders of the Lost Ark, including the scene in which Indiana Jones threatens to destroy the Ark with a bazooka. Just south of Dghoumès National Park is a desert oasis called Bouhlel Sdada, used for the archaeological dig scenes in Raiders.

3. Ajim (Mos Eisley)

Location: Ajim city center, Médenine Governorate, Djerba island, Tunisia

Start of totality and duration: 10:10 a.m. CET; 3 minutes, 55 seconds

Chance of clouds: 19%

Djerba Island's palm trees, beaches and Mediterranean horizons will make it a popular destination for eclipse chasers after a long totality away from the heat and crowds of Luxor in Egypt. It's also home to three notable Star Wars filming locations. The original movie's Mos Eisley footage was shot here, with Ajim doubling as a Stormtrooper checkpoint ("These are not the droids you're looking for"), the Cantina exterior, and an alley near Docking Bay 94 where stormtroopers watch the Millennium Falcon blast off. In reality, it's an abandoned bakery.

4. Amghar Mosque (Obi-Wan Kenobi's house)

Location: Ajim outskirts, Médenine Governorate, Djerba island, Tunisia

Start of totality and duration: 10:09 a.m. CET; 4 minutes

Chance of clouds: 19%

Just north of Ajim, this mosque — originally a fisherman's house — was used as a stand-in for "Old Ben's" house, where Obi-Wan Kenobi gives Luke Skywalker a lightsaber. It was used purely for photography, and no actors set foot here. It was also cut from the movie's Special Edition in 1997, so you'll only find it in the original version. Completists might also want to check out Sidi Jemour Mosque to the north, which was used for scenes with Biggs Darklighter that didn't even make the final cut. IYKYK …

How to go on a Star Wars tour in Tunisia

Tunisia's Star Wars locations are spread across the south, so the easiest way to see several is on an organized tour or with a private driver and guide. Tozeur is the main base for visiting Mos Espa, Ong Jemel and Jebel Sidi Bouhlel, with local operators offering half-day and full-day 4x4 excursions into the desert. Djerba Island is the other major hub for three sights. Longer multi-day tours typically connect Tozeur with Matmata, home to Hotel Sidi Idriss — the Lars Homestead — as well as Djerba.

One tour company, Star Wars Tours, is running a (sold-out) special departure called "Eclipse tour from the Outer Rim" that witnesses totality at the Mos Espa set. Other Star Wars-focused tour operators include Galaxy Tours, though one-day trips to the Mos Espa set from Tozeur are also available.

Where else to watch the eclipse in Tunisia

Tunisia is surely one of the most attractive destinations for the Aug. 2, 2027 total solar eclipse. Historical cloud cover is exceptionally low, while totality reaches around five and a half minutes near the centerline. It also offers established tourism infrastructure and generally lower August temperatures than Egypt, making it an obvious alternative for eclipse chasers hoping to avoid the biggest crowds around Luxor.

You can, of course, visit the Star Wars sets in the days before or after the eclipse. For Tunisia's maximum duration of totality, consider Sfax, where darkness lasts 5 minutes, 41 seconds, or nearby Chaffar Beach, with its long, open Mediterranean coastline. Offshore, the low-lying Kerkennah Islands get around 5 minutes, 39 seconds. Inland, Sidi Bouzid offers about 5 minutes, 33 seconds beneath typically dry skies, while the spectacular Roman amphitheater at El Jem gets 4 minutes, 23 seconds. On Djerba Island, meanwhile, beaches and extensive resort infrastructure make combining an eclipse chase with a conventional Mediterranean vacation particularly easy — with a view of Mos Eisley thrown in for good measure.

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Nov. 3, 1957: Laika the dog launches with Sputnik 2 ]]>

On Nov. 3, 1957, a Soviet space dog named Laika became the first animal to orbit Earth. Laika was a 3-year-old stray husky-spitz mix from the streets of Moscow, and she was recruited by the Soviet space program for her small size and calm temperament.

Unfortunately for Laika, this mission was a one-way trip. The Soviets didn't design a way to bring her back down to Earth. With only 7 days worth of oxygen and a little bit of food on board, Laika launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan with a Russian Sputnik rocket. This was the same kind of rocket used to launch the first Sputnik satellite.

Laika was alive when she reached orbit, but she died shortly afterward because the spacecraft's heat shield had broken off. Laika overheated before she had the chance to die of starvation of oxygen deprivation.

Why it mattered

Laika has remained one of space history's most beloved and tragic figures. People around the world have dogs as pets who they love as members of their own families. And even nearly 70 years after this flight, it is so heartbreaking to think of Laika on that frightening journey from which she never returned.

Laika was one of many different animals that were used in early spaceflight testing. Both the U.S. and Russia launched a number of primates on flights testing early flight technology. Sadly, like Laika, many of these brave creatures did not make it back.

Unbelievably, though, some did survive the journey. For example, the chimpanzee named Ham and nicknamed the "astrochimp" survived a 1961 test flight to space. Though, the team behind that flight was so unsure of how it would go that Ham didn't get his name until after it was found that he'd survived his return.

 <description>Ústecký krajský soud prohlásil hlasování ve volbách do zastupitelstva Moldavy na Teplicku za neplatné. Nezákonné bylo podle soudu to, že někteří voliči nebyli připuštěni k hlasování. <title>Programátoři už nestíhají kontrolovat, co píše AI. Vyřešit to chce open-source projekt, kterému teď pomáhají Češi</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/programatori-uz-nestihaji-kontrolovat-co-pise-ai-open-source-projekt-to-chce-resit-pomahaji-mu-cesi/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Pokud umělá inteligence přebírá část role programátorů a pí&#353;e kód, jehož množství navíc stále narůstá, kdo stihne kontrolovat umělou inteligenci? Stále palčivěj&#353;í otázku si vzal za svůj byznysplán polský startup e2e, který teď začali podporovat Če&#353;i. Jeho projekt &#8211; za pomocí AI agentů &#8211; software testuje. Je to open-source nástroj, pro vývojáře zdarma, který dokáže prověřovat webové i mobilní aplikace podobně jako běžný uživatel: projít přihlá&#353;ení, vyplnit formulář, vložit zboží do ko&#353;íku a dokončit objednávku.</description>

 <description>Čtvrtá vláda Roberta Fica (Směr) přišla o dosavadní nejtěsnější většinu v parlamentu. V něm nyní koaliční strany po dalším odchodu drží jen 75 ze 150 křesel.  <description>Sedmdesátiletá penzistka z ukrajinského Chersonu odmítá opustit město, na které každý den útočí ruská armáda. Babička ale odejít nechce, Cherson považuje za svůj domov a nemíní před Rusy ustupovat.</description>

Při přepočtu hlasů soud zjistil, že čtvrtina z nich nebyla do výsledku započtená. Při porovnání původních a přepočtených výsledků byly zjištěny podstatné rozdíly v počtech hlasů.</description></item><item><title>Jizerská 50 trhá rekordy, hlavní závod se vyprodal nejrychleji v historii</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/sport/904772-jizerska-50-trha-rekordy-hlavni-zavod-se-vyprodal-nejrychleji-v-historii.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/sport/904772-jizerska-50-trha-rekordy-hlavni-zavod-se-vyprodal-nejrychleji-v-historii.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 04 Nov 2026 10:45:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Sport</category><description>Jubilejní 60. ročník Jizerské 50 hlásí rekordní zájem. Kapacita hlavního závodu se naplnila za něco málo přes dva měsíce, rychle se plní také kratší tratě.</description></item><item><title>Liberečtí kriminalisté pátrají po uprchlém vězni. Nesnažte se ho zadržet, varují</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/904835-liberecti-kriminaliste-patraji-po-uprchlem-vezni-nesnazte-se-ho-zadrzet-varuji.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/904835-liberecti-kriminaliste-patraji-po-uprchlem-vezni-nesnazte-se-ho-zadrzet-varuji.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 04 Nov 2026 08:54:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Liberečtí policisté vyhlásili celostátní pátrání po 39letém vězni, který v neděli 1. listopadu utekl z pracoviště v ulici České Mládeže v Liberci. Může se pohybovat kdekoliv v regionu. Pokud muže spatříte, v žádném případě se ho nesnažte sami zadržet a ihned volejte tísňovou linku 158.</description></item><item><title>Geopark Český ráj přijde o značku UNESCO, nevyřešil problém s prodejem kamenů</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904834-geopark-cesky-raj-prijde-o-znacku-unesco-nevyresil-problem-s-prodejem.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904834-geopark-cesky-raj-prijde-o-znacku-unesco-nevyresil-problem-s-prodejem.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 04 Nov 2026 06:30:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Geopark Český ráj se sídlem v Turnově přijde na konci letošního roku o prestižní značku UNESCO, kterou má od roku 2015. O jeho vyloučení v úterý rozhodla na svém zasedání Rada globálních geoparků UNESCO. Geopark ji nepřesvědčil, že vyřešil problém s prodejem drahých kamenů nejasného původu.</description></item><item><title>KOMENTÁŘ: Investiční návyky Čechů nemění jen inflace. Velký vliv mají i generační rozdíly</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/blogy-a-komentare/904643-komentar-investicni-navyky-cechu-nemeni-jen-inflace-velky-vliv-maji-i-generacni-rozdily.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/blogy-a-komentare/904643-komentar-investicni-navyky-cechu-nemeni-jen-inflace-velky-vliv-maji-i-generacni-rozdily.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 03 Nov 2026 20:35:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Jan Dragon</dc:creator><category>Blogy a komentáře</category><description>Ekonomické otřesy posledních let, divoká inflace a skokový růst úrokových sazeb, nám všem daly tvrdou lekci. Ukázaly, že nechat úspory ležet na běžném účtu znamená sledovat, jak ztrácejí hodnotu. Čechy to donutilo přemýšlet jinak a celkový fondový kapitál u nás už přesáhl 2,33 bilionu korun.</description></item><item><title>Protest v Liberci: Stovky lidí bránily před radnicí nezávislost ČT a ČRo</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904828-protest-v-liberci-stovky-lidi-branily-pred-radnici-nezavislost-ct-a-cro.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904828-protest-v-liberci-stovky-lidi-branily-pred-radnici-nezavislost-ct-a-cro.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 03 Nov 2026 19:37:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Na náměstí Dr. E. Beneše se 3. listopadu v 16:36 sešly stovky lidí - od studentů přes seniory, herce i zástupce univerzity. Před libereckou radnicí vyjádřili rozhodnou podporu stávkujícím zaměstnancům České televize a Českého rozhlasu v jejich boji za zachování svobodných a nezávislých médií.</description></item><item><title>Liberec jede na cheeseburgerech. Rekordní objednávka McDonald's přesáhla tři tisíce korun</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904652-liberec-jede-na-cheeseburgerech-rekordni-objednavka-mcdonald-s-presahla-tri-tisice-korun.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904652-liberec-jede-na-cheeseburgerech-rekordni-objednavka-mcdonald-s-presahla-tri-tisice-korun.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 03 Nov 2026 17:57:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Společnost</category><description>Od dubna 2024 doručili kurýři Bolt Food z libereckých restaurací McDonald's přes 9 400 objednávek téměř čtyřem tisícům zákazníků. Nejprodávanější položkou je (ne)obyčejný cheeseburger a nejvíc objednávek padá v pátek a v sobotu večer.</description></item><item><title>Lov na divoká prasata v Jablonci: Město ve čtvrtek uzavře okolí Srnčího dolu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904759-lov-na-divoka-prasata-v-jablonci-mesto-ve-ctvrtek-uzavre-okoli-srnciho-dolu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904759-lov-na-divoka-prasata-v-jablonci-mesto-ve-ctvrtek-uzavre-okoli-srnciho-dolu.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 03 Nov 2026 16:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Ve čtvrtek 5. listopadu od 8 do 13 hodin proběhne v okolí Srnčího dolu v Jablonci nad Nisou lov černé zvěře. Cílem myslivců je zregulovat přemnožená divoká prasata, která v posledních týdnech poškozují sportovní areál. Město žádá obyvatele, aby v této době omezili pohyb ve vyznačené oblasti.</description></item><item><title>Opilý tatínek přišel do muzea s holčičkami. Na chodbě zvracel</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/904755-opily-tatinek-prisel-do-muzea-s-holcickami-na-chodbe-zvracel.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/904755-opily-tatinek-prisel-do-muzea-s-holcickami-na-chodbe-zvracel.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 03 Nov 2026 14:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Tak tenhle nedělní program se tatínkovi se dvěma malými dcerkami nevyvedl. Vyrazil s nimi do Státního muzea skla a bižuterie v Jablonci, jenže nebyl úplně ve formě a na chodbě této instituce se dokonce pozvracel. Zaměstnankyně tak na místo zavolala strážníky.</description></item><item><title>Na Frýdlantsku začnou práce na prvním z projektů financovaných z Fondu Turów</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904626-na-frydlantsku-zacnou-prace-na-prvnim-z-projektu-financovanych-z-fondu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/904626-na-frydlantsku-zacnou-prace-na-prvnim-z-projektu-financovanych-z-fondu.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 03 Nov 2026 13:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Ve Frýdlantském výběžku začne stavba desetikilometrového vodovodního přivaděče z Dětřichova do Frýdlantu na Liberecku za zhruba 103 milionů korun. Je to první ze čtyř projektů financovaných z Fondu Turów.</description></item></channel></rss>

]]> Mandava Jazz / Mandau Jazz 2026 – Iva Bittová & Duo Jedlinský–Fischer https://www.vybezek.eu/296291-mandava-jazz-mandau-jazz-2026-iva-bittova-duo-jedlinsky-fischer/ Thu, 29 Oct 2026 18:16:24 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=296291 Další večer u Kocoura – Mezinárodní hudební festival Mandava Jazz 2026 tentokrát ve středu 28. října 2026, opět ve varnsdorfském pivovaru Kocour, dorazila Iva Bittová a duo Jedlinský & Fischer.

Stejně jako nedávného Dana Bártu i Ivu Bittovou jsme už zažili několikrát (2011 na Vlčí hoře nebo 2017 v divadle). Vždy jako personu velmi osobitou, která si s nástrojem, hlasem a jazykem (nebo spíš jazyky, chvílemi to vypadalo na hudební esperanto-svahilštinu), dělá co chce. A vždy bravurně. Ačkoli ona sama je většinou tahákem na plakátech a v upoutávkách, sama sebe neupřednostňuje a dává spoustu prostoru všem, se kterými v tu kterou chvíli spolupracuje.

Iva Bittová – zpěv, housle; Jakub Jedlinský – akordeon, zpěv; Pavel Fischer – housle, zpěv

Inu, někdo je Fotograf a umí (snad) zachytit neuchopitelnou atmosféru, vyjádřit obrazem zážitek z hudby. Já mezi takové nepatřím, nejsem fotograf. Jsem jen přítomen.
